# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–11 (Complete – Updated 102)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Evening at Brighton following Dobbin's arrival; George and Dobbin in latter's room; fine brilliant moonlight night of May, warm and balmy; evening at Ship Inn earlier; morning visits to parents and Brighton to follow. Army ordered to Belgium before week's end; mobilization imminent from Chatham. Three weeks before French Emperor likely attacks.
- **Primary Locations**: London (Russell Square, Thames Street counting-house, Slaughters' hotel), Brighton (George-Amelia honeymoon, Rawdon-Rebecca residence, Jos Sedley's visit, Ship Inn), Mirecombe (Seena Orlwood—drowned in flood; Pebin Wexwood, Maric Lindson, Rozek Hollwood, Halan Hollwood, Isbin Hollwood, Orvie, Nynelle Stenworth, Seena Hollett; Wevie Lindner gave birth to Brenelle Brackwood, father Madan Brackwood), Chatham (embarkation point), Belgium (destination)

## Main Characters

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Role in Marriage**: Primary architect of reconciliation between George and Amelia; convinced both to proceed; urged George before Belgium orders; presented gold chain and watch to Amelia; groomsman
- **Confrontation with John Osborne - UNSUCCESSFUL**: Entered City counting-house on Thames Street; received cordial welcome; revealed Belgium deployment; urged reconciliation for charity's sake; argued George is "high-minded." Osborne erupted calling Amelia "swindling old bankrupt's daughter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up; said George should "buy a broom and sweep a crossing." Dobbin departed; later sent note to Osborne with Belgium information
- **Brighton Arrival and Actions**: Arrived via Slaughters' hotel; imparted Belgium news to Ensign Stubble (who purchased new sword); witnessed Stubble's tears writing to mother; locked his desk, resolving to visit parents then travel to Brighton. Dined with Ensign Stubble, Ensign Spooney, and Mr. Chopper at theatre box. At Ship Inn: assumed "jovial and rattling manner" to hide feelings upon seeing Mrs. George Osborne; made clumsy compliments; discussed Brighton, sea-air, gaieties
- **In Dobbin's Room with George - CURRENT**: Delivered lawyer's letter from Mr. Osborne containing disinheritance notice. George erupted in rage, calling marriage "d--d sentimentality," accusing Dobbin of ruining him; complained about financial ruin (lost £140 to Crawley at cards; £2,000 annuity insufficient for two years). Dobbin replied calmly: position is hard and partly his making; many captains have less; George must live on pay (£100/year for Amelia if he dies); encouraged George to remember he's now "a dethroned prince" and wait for tempest to pass; promised if George's name appears in Gazette, old father will relent; offered personal financial support if anything happens (claims he has "a little" and is "not a marrying man"); promised not to forget his godson in will. George forgave Dobbin generously, unable to stay angry long
- **Internal Conflict Intensified**: Deeply troubled by guilt over role in hastening marriage; believes his own unendurable suspense over Amelia drove him to crush uncertainty by hastening marriage; feels he is traitor to both father and son; ashamed Amelia is always first in his thoughts (before father, mother, sisters, duty—waking and sleeping, all day long); considers himself becoming "consummate hypocrite" daily, hiding private feelings and apprehensions
- **Reputation**: "Greatly respected in the regiment, as the best officer and the cleverest man in it"; backed young Stubble's courage; advised him to leave off brandy and water
- **Knowledge of Amelia's Opinion**: Knows Amelia considers him lisping, plain, homely-looking, exceedingly awkward and ungainly; acquiesces humbly; acknowledges "a time came when she knew him better, and changed her notions regarding him; but that was distant as yet"

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED, DISINHERITED**: Married Amelia late April without father's consent; at Brighton honeymoon; now disinherited by father's lawyer letter
- **Financial Ruin - NEW**: Receives £2,000 in 4 percent annuities (one-third of mother's estate); loses £140 to Rawdon Crawley at cards/billiards at Brighton; complains sum won't last two years; accustomed to comforts and position; cannot live on captain's pay plus £100/year widow's allowance for Amelia; views himself as "dethroned prince"
- **Military Orders**: Regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; faces "great and certain risk" and possible fatal outcomes
- **Behavior at Brighton**: Already suffering ennui; eager for others' company; spending time with Rebecca and Rawdon (gallivanting, driving, dining); leaves Amelia neglected; frequents Rawdon's quarters for cards/billiards before bed; considers himself good-looking and susceptible to Rebecca's flattery
- **Reaction to Disinheritance**: Erupted in rage at Dobbin, blamed him entirely for marriage and ruin; accused Dobbin of never being easy until he got George married and ruined; declared marriage was "d--d sentimentality"; questioned Dobbin's judgment; ultimately forgave Dobbin generously and declared impossible to stay angry with him long

**Amelia Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED, BRIDE**: Married to George late April; one week into marriage at Brighton
- **Emotional Crisis - NEW**: Troubled by Rebecca's wit, spirits, accomplishments; misgives about Rebecca as friend; observes George already suffering ennui and eager for others' society; trembles for future; doubts own worthiness as companion; tormented by guilt about forcing George into marriage and causing his disinheritance; blames herself for neglecting poor father; couches in great chair neglected while George and Rebecca gaze on calm ocean and Rawdon/Jos play backgammon; feels despair and remorse as "bitter companions"; views future as "dismal prospect"; feels too shy and unfit to navigate marriage alone without guide and protector; considers herself humble, foolish creature unworthy of clever, brilliant George
- **Honeymoon Status**: Only week married; already neglected by George; timid and mute in company of Rebecca while others rattle away together; windows flung open to balcony; warm, balmy evening with moonlight

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Rawdon Crawley; at Brighton; still dunned by creditors; relies on Miss Crawley's relenting
- **Relationship with George - NEW**: Calls him "Cupid"; flattered him about good looks many times; watches over him kindly at cards; threatens to tell Emmy of his wicked ways and naughty extravagant habits; brings him cigars and lights them (calculated maneuver perfected on Rawdon); finds him horrid dissipated wretch; he thinks her gay, brisk, arch, distinguee, delightful; outshines Amelia completely in little drives and dinners while George and Rawdon rattle away together
- **Analysis of Dobbin**: Within two hours of meeting him, understood his secret (adoration of Amelia) perfectly; does not like him and fears him privately; disliked him more for his adoration of Amelia; notes he is so honest that her arts and cajoleries do not affect him and he shrinks from her with instinctive repulsion; not above jealousy; nevertheless maintains respectful, cordial manner; vowed to love him sincerely; remembers him from Vauxhall; made little fun of him when ladies dressed for dinner; finds him "good-natured nincompoop and under-bred City man"

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER - FINAL ACTION TAKEN]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **Knowledge and Rage**: Upon learning George married Amelia (Sedley's daughter), erupted in fury; called George "d---- fool"; denounced Amelia as "swindling old bankrupt's daughter," "beggar's girl out of a gutter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up; threatened George should "buy a broom and sweep a crossing"
- **Post-Confrontation Actions - COMPLETED**: Retreated to study after dinner; locked door; retrieved mahogany escritoire containing all George's documents since childhood (prize copy-books, drawing-books, childhood letters with love to parents and requests for cake, letters mentioning "godpapa Sedley," letters from West Indies, tailor's bills, drafts, commission newspapers, childhood whip, locket of George's hair worn by his mother); examined papers—especially those mentioning John Sedley—with "curses quivering on livid lips" and "horrid hatred and disappointment" writhing in his heart; marked, docketed, tied papers with red tape, carefully catalogued with dates
- **Disinheritance - EXECUTED**: Commissioned lawyer to draft and deliver letter to George stating: Mr. Osborne abides by previous determination to reject George; George ceases to be member of family as consequence of marriage; determination is "final and irrevocable." Money expended upon George in minority and bills drawn far exceed George's entitlement (one-third of mother's estate = £2,000 in 4 percent annuities); Mr. Osborne waives all claim upon George's estate; payment of £2,000 annuities at day's value to be paid upon receipt. Letter delivered via Mr. Chopper to Dobbin for forwarding to George

**Miss Jane Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- Learned of George's marriage from Dobbin; felt violently agitated, nearly fainted; gathered composure and defended George; moved by Dobbin's words about Amelia's faithful heart; immediately spread news to Miss Maria and Miss Wirt; not displeased; Amelia rose in her estimation for spirit displayed; capable of generous forgiveness; present at Russell Square dinner

**Miss Maria Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- Learned of marriage from Jane; not displeased; calculated with Mr. Frederick Bullock that George's "folly" might result in disinheritance, making Maria worth thirty thousand pounds more; present at Russell Square dinner; received unusually bland and attentive treatment from Mr. Bullock

**Mr. Frederick Bullock** [CHARACTER]
- Junior partner of wealthy firm; man of the world; understood George's "folly" might result in disinheritance, making Maria worth thirty thousand pounds more; dined at Russell Square; showed amazement at marriage news; rendered "still and quiet" by Mr. Osborne's dark looks; unusually bland and attentive to Miss Maria during dinner; lacked heart to sit alone near "terrible old gentleman in the study"; accompanied ladies upstairs

**Ensign Stubble** [CHARACTER]
- Seventeen years old, about sixty-five inches high; rickety constitution impaired by premature brandy and water; undoubted courage and lion's heart; Light Bobs. Upon hearing Belgium news from Dobbin, purchased new sword instantly; posed, tried, bent, balanced weapon, shouting and stamping feet with energy. At Slaughters' wrote letter home to mamma; tears trickling down nose as he thought he might never see her again; eyes brightened when Dobbin praised his courage and advised leaving off brandy and water. Dined with Ensign Spooney, Captain Dobbin, and Mr. Chopper at theatre box

**Ensign Spooney** [CHARACTER]
- Tall youth; Grenadier Company (Captain Dobbin's); tried on new bearskin cap; dined at theatre box; afterwards went to Slaughters' and ordered famous dinner, wrote letters home

**Other Characters**: Jos Sedley (at Brighton, patronizes Dobbin with much dignity, engaged at backgammon with Rawdon evening of Amelia's despair), Rawdon Crawley (at Brighton, pays scarcely any attention to Dobbin, plays backgammon with Jos, drives and dines with George and Rebecca), Mrs. Bute Crawley (at Brighton as nurse to Miss Crawley), Miss Crawley (at Brighton, still refusing to relent), Mr. Chopper (dined with officers, delivered letter from Mr. Osborne, became intoxicated), John Sedley (ruined, cursed by John Osborne), Mrs. Sedley (Amelia's mother, neglected by Amelia), Ellan (scrubbing step, asked about rain)

## Critical Facts and Status

- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - COMPLETED, HONEYMOON ONGOING, FATHER EXECUTED DISINHERITANCE**: Married late April without father's consent; one week into marriage at Brighton; John Osborne commissioned lawyer to draft disinheritance letter; George now receives only £2,000 in annuities (one-third of mother's estate); determination "final and irrevocable"; household catastrophe complete
- **GEORGE'S FINANCIAL CRISIS - ACUTE**: Disinherited; receives £2,000 annuities insufficient for his habits; lost £140 to Rawdon at cards at Brighton; must live on captain's pay (~£100/year for Amelia if he dies); cannot maintain his position in world on pittance; complains bitterly to Dobbin who urges patience, suggests father may relent if George's name appears in Gazette
- **AMELIA'S EMOTIONAL CRISIS - ACUTE**: One week married; already observes George suffering ennui and attracted to Rebecca; trembles for future; tormented by guilt about forcing George to marry and causing his ruin and disinheritance; blames herself for neglecting parents; feels despair and remorse; views future as dismal prospect; feels shy, unfit to navigate marriage alone; considers herself unworthy of George
- **MILITARY CRISIS URGENT**: Regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; mobilization imminent from Chatham; three weeks before French Emperor likely attacks; soldiers facing "great and certain risk"
- **DOBBIN'S GUILT AND EMOTIONAL BURDEN**: Holds himself responsible for marriage and consequent ruin; George blamed him entirely; Dobbin acknowledges position is "partly of [his] making"; continues to harbor secret adoration of Amelia; considers himself increasingly hypocritical
- **REBECCA'S MANIPULATION OF GEORGE**: Flatters him about good looks; watches over him kindly at cards; threatens to tell Emmy of his wicked ways; lights his cigars with calculated effect; completely outshines Amelia in social settings; George thinks her gay, brisk, arch, distinguee, delightful
